ImageDescription.value: A bank of monitors in the control room for the Wendelstein 7-X stellarator at the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics. The screens show a variety of real-time diagnostic data, including graphs of plasma energy and density, electron temperature, and visual data from ECRH (Electron Cyclotron Resonance Heating) and thermal imaging cameras. This data is crucial for scientists to monitor and analyze the plasma during an experiment

Visiting this site allows students to study the history of nuclear energy, the consequences of the 1986 disaster, and current radiation safety protocols.
